newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk shares firm in thin trade as holiday begins.
newsitem.headline: Turk shares firm in thin trade as holiday begins.

text.p: Istanbul shares firmed in extremely thin morning trade as the market entered a a 6-1/2-day holiday at midday on Thurday, brokers said. The stock market will reopen on April 24.

The IMKB National-100 closed nine points, or 0.59 percent higher at 1,532 after moving between 1,516 and 1,533. Morning volume shrank to 5.66 trillion lira ($42.7 million) from Wednesday's 8.44 trillion ($63.7 million).

"The market lacked direction ahead of the holiday and because of uneasiness caused by the forthcoming National Security Council (MGK) meeting. I do not expect much activity after the holiday," said Haydar Haydaroglu from Halkbank.

The market is unnerved by the MGK meeting scheduled for April 26 following a rift which emerged between the coalition's Islamist and conservative wings after the secularist military demanded measures against rising Islamist activism in the February 28 MGK meeting.
"There may be a rise if political tension eases after the holiday and if trade volume increases. Otherwise, the market will continue to drift sideways," Haydaroglu said.
Over the week, the index gained 1.8 percent after last week's 4.1 percent loss. Delay in settlements of share transactions because of the holiday had triggered some buying earlier in the week.
